subject: Physics
description: Newton's laws, satellites, escape velocity, Kepler's laws

questions.stem: Newton's THIRD LAW of motion states:

options.option_text: To every action there is an equal and opposite reaction
An object at rest stays at rest unless acted on by force

questions.explanation: 3rd law — action-reaction pairs act on DIFFERENT bodies. 1st law = inertia (option C). 2nd law = F = dp/dt ≈ ma (option A). Energy conservation is a separate principle.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The ESCAPE VELOCITY from the Earth's surface is approximately:
questions.explanation: Escape velocity from Earth's surface ≈ 11.2 km/s (from formula v_e = √(2GM/R)). 7.9 km/s is the ORBITAL velocity for low-Earth orbit. Escape velocity from the Moon ~2.4 km/s. Light travels at 300,000 km/s (c).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: If the Earth SUDDENLY shrank to half its present radius while keeping its mass the same, the weight of a 50 kg person would:

options.option_text: Become 4 times (g' = GM/r'² with r' = r/2)

questions.explanation: g ∝ 1/r² (surface gravity for fixed mass). If r halves → g × 4. Weight = mg, so weight becomes 4×. (Mass is unchanged, but WEIGHT — the gravitational force — quadruples.)
questions.subject: Physics

options.option_text: Is always directly over the equator at altitude ~36,000 km, with a 24-hour orbital period

questions.explanation: Geostationary — equatorial orbit at ~35,786 km altitude; orbital period = Earth's rotation period (23h 56m) so the satellite stays over the same ground point. Used for TV broadcasting, weather. INSAT satellites of India are geostationary.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: An object is thrown vertically upward with velocity u. The maximum HEIGHT reached is:
questions.explanation: At max height, v = 0. Using v² = u² − 2gh → 0 = u² − 2gh → h = u²/(2g). Time to reach max height: t = u/g.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The ACCELERATION DUE TO GRAVITY (g) at the equator compared to the poles is:

options.option_text: Smaller at the equator (≈ 9.78 m/s² vs ≈ 9.83 m/s² at poles)

questions.explanation: g is SMALLER at the equator due to (a) centrifugal effect of rotation reducing effective g, (b) equatorial bulge (Earth isn't a perfect sphere — r is ~21 km larger at equator). Combined: equator g ~9.78, poles g ~9.83, standard g = 9.81 m/s².
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: KEPLER'S THIRD LAW states T² ∝ ?, where T is the orbital period:
questions.explanation: Kepler's 3rd law: T² = (4π²/GM) × a³ → T² ∝ a³. Hence inner planets (smaller a) have much shorter years; outer planets take far longer (Neptune: 165 years).
